[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] 6.14 Where the court is of the opinion that the decision appealed against was erroneous in point of law, it will not set aside or vary that decision but will remit the matter to the Secretary of State for re-hearing and determination in accordance with the opinion of the court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] 6.15 The court may give directions as to the exercise, until an appeal brought by virtue of section 289(1) of the TCP Act is finally concluded and any re-hearing and determination by the Secretary of State has taken place, of the power to serve, and institute proceedings (including criminal proceedings) concerning—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] (a)a stop notice under section 183 of that Act; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] (b)a breach of condition notice under section 187A of that Act. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54D – PLANNING COURT CLAIMS AND APPEALS TO THE PLANNING COURT > 6.11 The persons to be served with the appellant’s notice are—] 6.16 An appeal brought by virtue of sections 289(1) or (2) of the TCP Act or section 65(1) of the PLBCA Act will be treated as if it is a review under statute for the purposes of rules 45.41 to 45.44 and may therefore be an Aarhus Convention claim for the purposes of those rules.
